findings.why_it_matters: In GR 11's TIME table (ACCEPT statement) the sub-items a) and b) belong inside the 5-6 row's Contents cell, but the transcription closes the table after that row and sets them as free paragraphs. The 7-8 row then falls out of the table as an indented text line. All the words are kept, but the table no longer shows that a) and b) qualify positions 5-6, and position 7-8 is no longer a table row.

findings.why_it_matters: The ACCEPT GR 13 table of screen-item categories and their figurative constants is one table in the PDF. The transcription splits it in two: the Alphanumeric-edited row falls out as loose text, and the second table makes 'Boolean | ZEROS' its header row. A reader or tool that parses the tables loses the Alphanumeric-edited mapping and treats Boolean as a column heading.

ADD GR 1 (standard arithmetic): the subscripts 1, 2 and n on operand-1 are flattened into the name, so the expression reads as operands named operand-11, operand-12 and operand-1n instead of the 1st, 2nd and nth instances of operand-1.

ADD GR 2 (format 2, standard arithmetic): the same lost-subscript error turns the indexed operand-1 instances into names such as operand-11 and operand-12, which could be mistaken for distinct operands.
